message.content:
The Battle of Waterloo (18 June 1815) was one of the bloodiest single-day engagements of the Napoleonic Wars.  In total, the combined casualties for the French and the Anglo‑Dutch‑Prussian coalition were roughly **23 000–24 000** men.  

| Side | Approximate casualties (killed, wounded, missing) |
|------|---------------------------------------------------|
| French | 25 000–27 000 |
| Anglo‑Dutch‑Prussian coalition | 22 000–23 000 |

These figures come from contemporary reports and later military historians.  The numbers vary slightly depending on the source, but most modern accounts settle on the 23 000–24 000 range for the overall loss of life and wounded.
